issues.display_title: Issue #864: fix(editor): a room's type and colour are keyed by its position in the detected list
issues.main_description_html:
Found while reviewing #860. Not caused by it — #860 makes it easier to reach, and the same PR fixed the sibling shear on the store id but deliberately left this one alone because it needs a persistence decision.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

A room's type (closed, hallway, open-to-below) and colour live in model.areaMeta, keyed by the room's position in the detectRooms output:

// src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/model-sync.ts
const metaKey = r.manual ? r.key : String(i);

detectRooms sorts by area, largest first. So drawing a room whose area sorts into the MIDDLE of the list slides every room after it one seat along, and each one inherits its neighbour's type and colour.

Verified: three rooms of 10000 / 3600 / 1600 with areaMeta {"0": hall, "1": {type:"closed", color:"#e11"}, "2": {type:"hallway"}}. Draw one 70×70 loop and detectRooms returns 10000 / 4900 / 3600 / 1600. recomputeRooms only ever ADDS a missing key, never remaps, so areaMeta["1"] — Closed, #e11 — now describes the new 4900 room; the 3600 room inherits hallway and loses both its Closed flag and its colour.

Closed is not cosmetic: closedRoomAt / blockingClosedArea gate every add-tool, so objects can now be placed in a room the user sealed, and are refused in one they never touched.

The key scheme is written out in four places that cannot import each other: model-sync.ts (metaKey), commands.ts (areaMetaKey), bridge.ts (metaOf), hittest.ts (a copy, blocked by a cycle).

Why #860 raises it

Before #860, a newly resolved room was appended to the end of the list on purpose (#849) exactly to avoid this. #860 detects rooms as graph faces and sorts the whole list by area, so a new room lands where its size puts it. A room the user draws has always been able to land mid-list, so this is not new — but it is now the ordinary case rather than the awkward one.

Note the load path is already safe: levelToModel pairs each stored area to its room by geometry (#860), so areaMeta starts a session correctly keyed. The shear happens to rooms that appear during a session.

Scope

Give areaMeta an identity that survives the list reordering. Candidates, in the order they look cheapest:

  1. Remap on recompute. recomputeRooms already has the previous ctx.rooms and the new one; pair them the way pairByGeometry (bridge.ts) pairs stored areas to rooms, and rewrite the keys. Contained to one function, no format change, but the mapping is lost across a reload — which is fine, because the load path re-seeds from the store.
  2. Key by geometry instead of position — the same d:round(cx):round(cy) the room height uses, which #860 already made a shared helper (roomKey). One scheme instead of two, and it survives a reload. Needs a migration for stored areaMeta and a decision about nested rooms, whose centroids can coincide.

Whichever is picked, the four copies of the key scheme should end up reading one helper.

Tests

recomputeRooms keeps each room's type and colour when a new room appears ahead of it in the sorted list; a Closed room stays Closed across an undo of an unrelated edit; closedRoomAt still refuses placement in the room the user actually sealed. src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/ holds the model-sync and command cases.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

Correction — re-checked against 83faa3c (2026-09-01)

The defect is real and still present; I reproduced it end to end. Four claims above are wrong.

1. "Four places that cannot import each other" is false. All four sites already import the ../floorplan barrel, and roomKey is exported from it (floorplan/index.ts:16). Collapsing the key scheme into one helper next to roomKey costs one function and four one-line call-site edits, with no new import edge and no cycle to solve. The hittest → commands cycle noted at hittest.ts:302-306 is real (commands.ts:10 imports findAnno/closedRoomAt from hittest) but irrelevant — the helper does not have to live in commands.ts. Delete that comment with the fix. eslint.config.mjs has no import/no-cycle rule, so nothing enforces it either way.

2. There is a fifth positional site. src/components/editor/floorplan-editor/SelectionToolbars.tsx:89 — lvl?.layout.areas[selectedRoomIndices[0]]. The type picker's active state and the Closed-room colour swatch read the store's areas by the engine's room index, so the user sees the sheared type on the wrong room. commands.ts:64-66 already flags this coupling as load-bearing.

3. The load path is faithful, not healing. levelToModel's geometry pairing (bridge.ts:264-281) does survive a reversed area order — verified. But modelToLevel writes the sheared type onto the wrong room's stored area first (...metaOf(String(rawIndex), pa), bridge.ts:482), so the damage is persisted, not transient: a reload reproduces it exactly. "The load path is already safe" should read "the load path does not add new shear".

4. Fix option 1 is not contained to one function. pairByGeometry (bridge.ts:121) and pairingHolds (bridge.ts:89) are module-private and typed against the store's AreaLayer, not Room. Two ways out:

  • (a) export them from bridge.ts and widen the param to readonly { boundaries: number[][] }[] — they only ever read .boundaries, so it is a signature change with no body change. Cost: a new editor/ → bridge import edge, a direction that does not exist today (no cycle: bridge's only editor/ import is the leaf constants.ts).
  • (b) preferred — move pairingHolds, pairByGeometry and interiorPoint (bridge.ts:89-166) down into floorplan/geometry.ts. They are pure geometry already using only polygonAreaAndCenter, pointInPolygon and labelPoint, all of which live there. bridge.ts then imports them from the barrel it already imports, and model-sync gets them with no new edge at all. ~50 lines relocated, zero logic change.

Fix option 2 confirmed expensive. roomKey is the rounded centroid, so two concentric rooms key identically — verified: detectRooms on a 100×100 containing a concentric 40×40 yields two rooms with the same roomKey string. migrateRoomHeights (bridge.ts:313) already lives with this collision for heights and resolves it by refusing to guess, so a new keying scheme needs the same escape hatch — it cannot be a pure key swap.

Extra constraints for the implementation

  • The remap must be idempotent. history.ts:12 snapshots areaMeta and :125 restores it wholesale, and the remap runs inside recomputeRooms, which also runs after an undo. If it is not idempotent against a restored snapshot, Ctrl+Z re-shears. The #735 cases at model-sync.test.ts:170-185 are the fence.
  • Hot path. pairByGeometry is O(rooms × areas) with a bbox reject. Today it runs twice, at bridge crossings; recomputeRooms runs after every geometry edit. Sanity-check a large imported mall plan before merging.
  • Decide: fix areaMeta alone (the placement guard is the safety-relevant half) or re-key SelectionToolbars.tsx:89 too. Fixing only areaMeta leaves the type picker able to display the wrong room's type while the guard behaves correctly.
  • Product call: when geometry stops recognising a room (past the pairingHolds threshold), should its Closed type be dropped the way the Information link already is (bridge.ts:465, the #798 gate), or carried positionally? Dropping silently un-seals a room the user sealed; carrying re-introduces a smaller version of this bug.

Tests that pin it

In src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/model-sync.test.ts, beside describe("recomputeRooms seeds areaMeta (#735)"):

  • three disjoint squares 10000/3600/1600 with areaMeta = {"0": hallway, "1": {type:"closed", color:"#e11"}, "2": hallway}; push a 70×70 loop (4900) and recomputeRooms. Assert rooms.map(r => r.area) is [10000, 4900, 3600, 1600], then that closedRoomAt at the 3600 centre is still that room and at the 4900 centre is null. Both invert today.
  • assert areaMeta after the recompute equals the pre-state plus only "3": {type:null,color:null} — passes today and must keep passing, so a remap does not stop the seed loop working.

Through the real bridge (area-lifecycle.test.ts or a new roundtrip-area-meta.test.ts):

  • modelToLevel on the sheared model, indexed by computed area — assert the 3600 area carries closed/#e11. Fails today; confirmed reverse is {10000: hallway, 4900: closed/#e11, 3600: hallway, 1600: null}. This is the assertion proving the damage is persisted.
  • levelToModel with layout.areas reversed still lands areaMeta on the right rooms — passes today, fences the load path.
  • a manual Area with areaMeta["m:A1"] round-tripped with an extra room added in between comes back unchanged — fences the m:<id> path against a remap that treats all keys alike.

RESULT

Done on branch feature/864-areameta-identity, commit 7f29569. Not pushed — waiting for approval.

recomputeRooms now re-keys areaMeta onto the new indices instead of only seeding missing ones. Rooms are paired by geometry with the same pairByGeometry / pairingHolds the bridge already uses, so an entry moves with its own room. A room that grew or shrank past PAIR_AREA_TOLERANCE pairs with nothing and its type is dropped rather than transplanted — the call modelToLevel already makes for the Information link (#798): a missing type is visible and re-settable, a misplaced one is invisible and wrong.

Those two helpers were module-private in bridge.ts and typed against the store's AreaLayer, so they moved down to floorplan/geometry.ts beside the polygonAreaAndCenter / pointInPolygon / labelPoint they already use, taking a structural Ring instead. Pure relocation, no logic change, and the engine reaches them without the editor gaining a dependency on the bridge.

Re-keying is wrong wherever the model is swapped rather than edited — the incoming map is already keyed to its own geometry, and pairing it against whatever ctx.rooms was left holding would scramble a correct map. Three callers opt out: history restore, applyModel, and the adoptBackdropSize re-scale (which moves every area by the square of the scale factor). Stacked floors of one building share a footprint, so a level switch there is not merely lossy — it crosses types between floors.

The key scheme itself was spelled out in five places, each with a comment asking the next reader to keep them in step. It is now detectedMetaKey / manualMetaKey next to roomKey.

Corrections to the task body

Three claims above turned out wrong and are corrected in the "Correction — re-checked against 83faa3c" section:

  • "four places that cannot import each other" is false. All four already import the floorplan barrel where roomKey lives, so the shared helper needed no new import edge and no cycle to solve.
  • The load path is faithful, not healing. modelToLevel writes the sheared type onto the wrong room's stored area (bridge.ts:482), so a reload reproduced the damage exactly.
  • There is a fifth positional site, SelectionToolbars.tsx:89. It needs no change: it reads the array modelToLevel builds in the same order, so it was wrong only because areaMeta was, and is right again for the same reason.

Files changed

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/model-sync.ts — the re-key, and the rekeyAreaMeta opt-out
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts — pairingHolds, pairByGeometry, interiorPoint, Ring (relocated)
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/rooms.ts — detectedMetaKey, manualMetaKey
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts — imports the relocated helpers; local copies deleted
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/commands.ts, hittest.ts, history.ts — use the shared key; the "can't import" comment deleted
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/__tests__/area-meta-rekey.test.ts — new, 9 cases

Verified

  • pnpm test — 215 files, 2001 passed, 3 skipped
  • pnpm lint — 0 errors (1 pre-existing warning in geometry.ts, unrelated, arrived with #860)
  • pnpm exec tsc --noEmit — clean

Every guard is mutation-checked individually: disabling the re-key fails five cases, and each of the three opt-outs, the manual-key passthrough and the empty-previous guard fails exactly one. Two of my first attempts were weak and the mutation pass is what caught them — one probe point sat on a room boundary, and two opt-outs had no coverage at all.

Demo

.playwright-mcp/demo/864/video-864-areameta-identity.mp4 — 1920×1080, 60 fps, 2:20. Measured both ways first: on development the sealed room reads Room and takes a point; on this branch it stays Closed and refuses. See the demo comment for the table.

Note

Merges cleanly with feature/865-convert-duplicate-walls apart from one import line each in floorplan/index.ts and editor/commands.ts. Trial-merged and tested: 2012 passed together.

issues.display_title: Issue #865: fix(editor): Convert To Room duplicates a wall that is already there
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

video-865-wall-reuse.mp4

Found while reviewing #860, on the project the Convert To Room reports came from (23839d5f-5390-45e8-9cb1-3109bf7d65d8).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

convertAreaToRoom (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/commands.ts) generates one wall per polygon edge and appends them, without looking at what is already there:

for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
  const a = pts[i], b = pts[(i + 1) % n];
  edges.push({ x1: a[0], y1: a[1], x2: b[0], y2: b[1], l: "0", r: "0" });
}

On a Mappedin import, neighbouring tenants' rings run along the same physical wall but are not identical — they differ by a unit or two. Converting both leaves two walls where there is one wall, and the space between them is a real enclosed face.

Measured on that project, converting every Area in turn: level 2 goes to 8 216 walls and 565 rooms against 401 Areas. #860 filters out anything thinner than the node tolerance, which removed the worst of it (the smallest face went from 1 unit² to 9), but 14 faces under 25 unit² survive on a plan 23 597 units across. Each one is a store AreaLayer with an id, a row in the object list, a polygon on the map and a search/routing target.

Scope

Stop generating a wall that duplicates one already in the model. For each generated edge, if an existing wall lies along it — collinear within tolerance and overlapping its span — reuse that wall instead of adding a second one, extending it where the new edge runs past its end.

Do it in the same dry run that already exists, so a conversion that would produce nothing new still refuses before mutating anything, and pushUndo still reverses a single step.

Related decision, worth settling in the same task: whether two Areas that shared a boundary before the conversion should end up sharing a wall afterwards. They should — that is what makes the two rooms neighbours rather than two rooms with a crack between them.

Not this task

The faces that remain after de-duplication are what the walls genuinely enclose; #860 deliberately has no minimum room size beyond the node tolerance, and that should stay. This is about not creating the duplicate wall, not about hiding what a duplicate produces.

Tests

Converting an Area whose ring runs along an existing wall adds no second wall and produces no sliver room; converting two Areas that share a boundary leaves them sharing one wall; a conversion that adds nothing at all still refuses without mutating the model. src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/convert-area-to-room.test.ts.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

Correction — re-checked against 83faa3c (2026-09-01)

Still accurate; the quoted code is unchanged (git log -- commands.ts shows nothing since). Two corrections and one number the task is missing.

1. "The space between them is a real enclosed face" is only sometimes true. It holds when the divergence is enclosed at both ends and wider than 1 unit mean width. #860 has two mitigations, both on TOL = 1 (rooms.ts:58): coincident chords collapse onto one graph edge (rooms.ts:220-231), and area2 / perim < TOL drops sliver faces (rooms.ts:338 — 2·area/perimeter, "not a room", not an area minimum). Measured: an Area ring laid exactly over an existing room goes 4 → 8 walls with the room count unchanged — a duplicate wall record and nothing else. A ring detouring 2.5 units off a 20-unit stretch goes 4 → 9 walls and 1 → 3 rooms, the extra one 25 unit². At a 1.5-unit detour, no phantom room. So the body's "14 faces under 25 unit² survive" is consistent with a 1-unit mean-width floor, but the duplicate wall is the primary cost and the phantom face is the secondary one.

2. The identical missing guard is in finishWall (interaction-tools.ts:122) — that is #872, now tracked as #880. commands.ts:265 and interaction-tools.ts:122 are the only two walls.push sites in the engine and both are missing the same lookup. Write the shared helper once; whichever task lands first owns it and the other becomes call-site wiring plus tests.

3. The reuse tolerance is unset and cannot be derived from the code. It must be larger than TOL = 1 to do anything at all — at 1 unit the endpoints already fuse and edgeAt already collapses the edge — and above 1 unit it welds geometry the user can see as two walls. ~2–3 units catches the Mappedin divergence described. Pick a number, put it next to TOL, and state what it costs.

Reuse the existing primitive

doorSpanOnWall (geometry.ts:264) is already the "collinear and overlapping" helper — normalised-cross parallelism (cross > 0.2 reject) plus per-endpoint perpendicular distance, wrapped as wallForOpening (editing.ts:31). It clips its span to [0,1], so a reuse check that must also extend should call the primitive underneath, projectOnWall (geometry.ts:253). Do not grow a fourth copy.

Shape of the change in convertAreaToRoom: between building edges (:242) and the dry run (:253), produce two lists — newEdges and { wall, x1, y1, x2, y2 } extensions. Feed the reconciled set to the existing detectRooms trial at :253 (it already builds a throwaway array, so this costs nothing structurally), then after pushUndo apply the extensions in place and push only newEdges. Skip curved walls: splitWallAt:101 already guards h1x !== undefined and a bezier has no straight span to extend.

Safe by construction

  • Wall ids are positional (bridge.ts:368 maps model.walls 1:1 by index) — extending in place preserves the index and therefore the id; skipping a push only appends fewer walls, no splice, no reindex.
  • wallForOpening / doorSpanOnWall clip to [0,1], so a door on the original span still resolves after the wall is lengthened. setWallWidth writes by index — preserved.
  • Undo is a whole-model JSON snapshot (history.ts:12, restore at :120) under the single pushUndo already at commands.ts:263.
  • closedWallOwners (map/geojson-utils.ts) attributes walls to closed rooms by geometry — a lengthened wall can newly count as another closed room's boundary and pick up its tint. And extending a wall can move a real room's centroid by a unit and orphan its stored height; migrateRoomHeights (bridge.ts:313) exists for exactly that and moves an orphan only when the match is unambiguous.

Two rulings this task assumes but should not

  1. "A conversion producing nothing new still refuses." This is new behaviour and probably the wrong call. Converting an Area laid exactly over an existing room produces zero new walls, the dry run still finds the room, and today it succeeds — dropping the redundant Area and transferring the name, which is arguably right. Turning that into a refusal is a decision, not a consequence of the fix.
  2. "Two Areas that shared a boundary should share a wall afterwards." This follows for free from reuse — but it means deleting that one wall then opens both rooms. Correct digital-twin semantics, and worth stating out loud.

Tests — measured, not guessed

src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/convert-area-to-room.test.ts already has the ctxWith harness; it needs a variant taking a starting wall list.

  1. No duplicate wall. Existing square (0,0)-(200,0)-(200,200)-(0,200); Area ring [[0,0],[200,0],[200,200],[0,200]]. Today walls.length === 8; assert 4.
  2. No phantom sliver. Same square; ring [[0,0],[10,-2.5],[20,0],[20,-60],[0,-60]]. Today non-manual rooms are 3 with areas [25, 1175, 40000]; assert 2 and no 25 unit² face.
  3. Reuse extends, does not truncate. Existing wall (0,0)-(100,0); ring [[0,0],[200,0],[200,100],[0,100]]. Assert wall 0 still starts (0,0) and now ends x2: 200, and walls.length === 4, not 5.
  4. Undo is one step. After case 1, undo(ctx) restores walls.length === 4 with original coordinates and manualAreas.length === 1 — guards the extension against escaping the single pushUndo.
  5. Refusal mutates nothing. Extend the existing self-crossing case at :81 with expect(ctx.model!.walls).toEqual(before), so reconciliation cannot leak a mutation ahead of the dry run.

Unrelated, noticed while tracing

src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/zz-probe.test.ts, zz-probe2.test.ts and src/lib/floorplanEditor/__tests__/zz-verify.test.ts are tracked in git (added by 1deb7ff) and are assertion-free console.log probes left from #839/#860. They run on every pnpm test. Worth their own cleanup — do not fold into this task.

RESULT

Done on branch feature/865-convert-duplicate-walls, commit 0c3e11a. Not pushed — waiting for approval.

Each generated edge is now reconciled against the existing walls before anything is committed. An edge lying along a wall folds into it; an edge running past its end extends it rather than being clipped or duplicated; an edge matching nothing is built as before.

reusableWall in floorplan/geometry.ts is the one implementation, sitting beside projectOnWall and doorSpanOnWall so it can also be called from finishWall — #880 is this same defect at the drawing tool, and wiring it there is now the call site plus its tests.

The test is collinearity, not parallelism: both endpoints within tolerance of the wall's infinite line means the edge runs along it over its whole length, which is what "the same wall" means and what an angle test only approximates. A wall on that same line but past the edge's end is a different wall and is left alone.

Reconciliation runs against a copy, and against the reconciled copy rather than the original, so two ring edges lying on one long wall both fold into it and the second sees what the first did. The dry run then validates the walls the commit will actually build, and only after it passes does pushUndo snapshot — so a refusal still mutates nothing and one Ctrl+Z still reverses the whole conversion, extension included.

Safe by construction: wall ids are positional, so reshaping in place keeps a wall's id and its openings (wallForOpening and doorSpanOnWall both clip to the wall's own span), and pushing fewer walls only shortens the array from the end. Curved walls are skipped — a bezier has no straight span to share, the same guard splitWallAt keeps.

The tolerance is the decision in this task

WALL_REUSE_TOL = 3. It must exceed TOL = 1 or it changes nothing visible — at one unit the endpoints already fuse and detectRooms already collapses the two chords onto one edge. Three is what the measurement asks for: what survived #860's mean-width floor on the reported import were faces up to 25 unit², a 2.5-unit detour over a 20-unit stretch. Two units leaves those.

The cost, stated plainly: a partition deliberately drawn three units from an existing wall now becomes that wall. If that is ever reported, this is the number to lower — and the sliver faces come back with it.

One thing deliberately NOT done

The task asked that a conversion producing nothing new should refuse. It currently succeeds and I have left it succeeding: an Area laid exactly over an existing room still resolves, and dropping the redundant Area and transferring its name is what the user asked for. Refusing there is new behaviour, not a consequence of this fix. Two-line change if the ruling goes the other way.

Correction to the task body

"The space between them is a real enclosed face" is only sometimes true — it holds when the divergence is enclosed at both ends and wider than one unit mean width. An Area laid exactly over an existing room goes 4 → 8 walls with the room count unchanged: a duplicate wall record and nothing else. The duplicate wall is the primary cost; the phantom face is the secondary one.

Files changed

  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts — reusableWall, WALL_REUSE_TOL, WallReuse
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/index.ts — exports
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/commands.ts — reconciliation in convertAreaToRoom
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/convert-area-to-room.test.ts — 10 new cases

Verified

  • pnpm test — 214 files, 2003 passed, 3 skipped
  • pnpm lint — clean (the pre-existing Wall unused-import warning is gone: reusableWall uses the type)
  • pnpm exec tsc --noEmit — clean

Every guard mutation-checked: removing reuse fails five cases, never extending fails three, not committing the extension and the overlap floor fail one each. The tolerance is pinned from both sides — at 2 the widest measured divergence stops folding, at 10 a wall drawn six units away gets welded.

Demo

.playwright-mcp/demo/865/video-865-wall-reuse.mp4 — 1920×1080, 60 fps, 1:56. The same scenario run against development fails on its first assertion: Convert To Room changed the wall count 34 -> 38. On this branch it stays 34.

issues.display_title: Issue #877: fix(projects): an empty project is never marked complete — the dashboard hides it and the cleanup job deletes it (#869)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-877.mp4

Implementation task for bug #869. The report is a screen recording with no text; the repro below is read frame by frame off that video, and the mechanism is traced in code.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Repro

  1. Dashboard shows 11 projects · 8 published · 3 drafts.
  2. + New Project → Create an empty project → name test empty project, address 50 Halsey Ave, East York, ON M4B 1A5, lat/lng filled → Create.
  3. Lands on /editor/88a4354b-e897-4b56-843f-59f050645e2e. Panel shows the name and address, Floor 1, All 0. Header: Saved just now.
  4. Draw two rectangles → All 10 (Room 1, Room 2, Wall 1–8). Header cycles Saving… → Saved just now. The 3D preview renders both rooms.
  5. Project menu → Dashboard.
  6. Dashboard is unchanged: still 11 projects · 8 published · 3 drafts, and test empty project is in neither the Recent rail nor the full All 11 list.

What actually happens

The project is created and is persisted. It is born with is_complete = false, and every dashboard query filters that out.

NewProjectFlow.submit() awaits createProject(...) and navigates on success — that is the whole path:

// src/components/projects/NewProjectFlow.tsx:148-159
const project = await createProject({ name, locationAddress, locationLat, locationLng })
reportCreated("ok")
router.push(`/editor/${project.id}?empty=1`)

createProject POSTs /v1/projects, throws on !res.ok, and returns the parsed body (src/actions/projects.ts:90-110) — so the UUID is server-generated and reaching the editor proves the row exists. The Go side builds the project without touching IsComplete (create.go:41-49), so it takes gorm:"not null;default:false" (models.go:76).

is_complete is set to true in exactly one place in this repo:

// src/lib/wizard/completeWizard.ts:63
updateProject(projectId, { ...fields, isComplete: true }).catch(() => {});

completeWizard is called only from the three wizard exits (StepGenerate ×2, StepUploadFloor import, and the generate latch at useWizardPersistence.ts:345). The empty-project modal never calls it, and nothing else in the repo ever sends isComplete. It is the one createProject caller with no completion stamp.

Both list endpoints filter unconditionally:

// list.go:57
q = q.Where("is_complete = ?", true)
// recent.go:39
Where("(user_id = ? OR id IN (?)) AND last_opened_at IS NOT NULL AND is_complete = ?", ..., true)

list.go:57 arrived in 7fc16ad ("hide incomplete projects by default in list endpoint") and is on both development and main. Nothing frontend-side can hide a listed project — useDashboard.ts:93-101 sends no status param, uses cache: "no-store", and derives the counts straight from the returned array. Hence 11 → 11.

The editor is honest about all of it: getProject has no completeness filter, so the panel renders; autosave's updateProject(id, {status:"edited"}) and saveFloorplanAction both return 200, and setLastSavedAt only runs after both succeed (EditorTopbar.tsx:112-137). "Saved just now" is true — the writes really landed on a row the dashboard will never show.

Severity: this is data loss, not a display bug

// jobs/eligibility.go:9-17
const cleanupThreshold = 24 * time.Hour
func isCleanupEligible(p models.Project, now time.Time) bool {
	if p.IsComplete { return false }
	return now.Sub(p.CreatedAt) >= cleanupThreshold
}

jobs/cleanup_incomplete_projects.go:42-55 soft-deletes every is_complete = false project older than 24h. Every empty project created since this modal shipped is destroyed the next day. Deletes are soft (models.go:15 gives Base a gorm.DeletedAt), so they are recoverable — worth checking production for is_complete = false rows with non-empty canvas_data before this lands, and deciding whether to restore them.

Scope

Do this. In NewProjectFlow.submit(), stamp the project complete before navigating:

const project = await createProject({ ... })
const marked = await updateProject(project.id, { isComplete: true })   // check .ok — it returns a result, it does not throw
reportCreated(marked.ok ? "ok" : "error")
router.push(`/editor/${project.id}?empty=1`)

Do not reuse completeWizard() here — it also writes gf_project_id, deletes the unkeyed wizard blob and fires a wizard_completed analytics event. This flow is not the wizard, and that event would pollute the #698 funnel with a phantom completion.

Consider alongside it, not instead of it. EditorTopbar.tsx:115 — widen the autosave patch to updateProject(id, { status: "edited", isComplete: true }). That closes the root cause at the seam every editor save routes through, so a future entry point that opens the editor outside the wizard is covered too. It does not cover "create an empty project and leave without drawing" (no edit ⇒ no autosave ⇒ still invisible, still reaped), and note saveNow skips the updateProject call entirely when projectStatus === "published".

Rejected. Dropping the is_complete filter from List/Recent, or from the create path. The flag exists to hide abandoned wizard drafts (the comments at list.go:16 and recent.go:36 cite FE bug #333) and it drives the cleanup job. Removing it re-opens #333.

Tests

src/components/projects/__tests__/NewProjectFlow.test.tsx already mocks @/actions/projects and next/navigation. Extend the mock with updateProject, fill name + coordinates, submit, then assert:

  • expect(updateProject).toHaveBeenCalledWith("new-id", expect.objectContaining({ isComplete: true })) — fails today with 0 calls, which is the whole bug in one line
  • router.push fired with /editor/new-id?empty=1 after it

If the autosave half is taken too, src/components/editor/__tests__/EditorTopbar.autosave.test.tsx already destructures the patch at lines 63-64 — add expect(patch).toMatchObject({ status: "edited", isComplete: true }).

Acceptance criteria

  • A project created through Create an empty project appears in the dashboard list and the Recent rail without a reload, and the header counts go up
  • It survives the 24h incomplete-project cleanup
  • reportCreated reports error if the completion stamp fails, so analytics never counts a project the dashboard cannot show
  • Wizard-created projects are unaffected; an abandoned wizard draft is still hidden and still reaped (#333 does not regress)
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Needs a ruling

  1. Is an empty project "real" the moment it is created, or once it has geometry? That is the choice between stamping at creation and stamping on first save. Stamping at creation is what this task assumes.
  2. is_complete currently means two things — "the wizard finished" (its origin, #333/#436) and "this project is real, show it and don't reap it". The empty-canvas flow has no wizard to finish. Either the flag gets split, or every non-wizard creator has to remember to stamp it — which is exactly the failure mode that produced this bug.
  3. Is CLEANUP_INCOMPLETE_PROJECTS_ENABLED on in production? That decides whether existing empty projects are merely invisible or already reaped.

Not this task

#868 / #870 (the empty-project tip's invisible click shield, shipped as 6bd302f) — different component, different failure, already merged.

Verification

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

issues.display_title: Issue #878: feat(editor): add, preview, change and remove a floor's image from the Edit Floor modal (#871)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-878.mp4

Implementation task for enhancement #871, checkbox 1: "Add image, preview image, change image, remove image floor".

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Context

There is one Edit Floor modal — src/components/setup/step-list-floor/EditFloorModal.tsx. Wizard Step 3 mounts it directly (StepListFloor.tsx:222-256); the editor mounts the identical component through the thin glue wrapper EditLevelModal.tsx:116-128, opened by the gear button in EditorPanel.tsx:160-169. So the screenshot in #871 is both surfaces at once, and one file covers both.

Each floor row today is: FloorThumbnail → NameField → truncated filename caption → HeightField → DeleteButton → drag grip (EditFloorModal.tsx:210-262). The thumbnail is read-only — the modal renders it without onPreview, so FloorThumbnail degrades to a plain div:

// src/components/setup/shared/FloorThumbnail.tsx:104-109
if (!onPreview) {
  return (<div className={v.frame} style={v.frameStyle}>{content}</div>);
}

There is no add, change or remove control anywhere in the modal. A floor's image is set in exactly two places — the wizard's Step 2 upload seeding floorConfigs (StepListFloor.tsx:62-89) and the editor's Add Floor (useAddLevel.ts:80-106) — and after creation nothing in the app ever changes it again: every updateFloorConfig caller passes only {name} or {height}.

The plumbing already exists — this is a UI task

  • The data model is three fields on FloorConfig (useMapStore.types.ts:24-32): fileUrl (render), serverPath (server reference), originalFileName (display). No File is stored, per the repo rule.
  • Upload: uploadProjectImage(file, projectId) (src/lib/editor/uploadImage.ts:8-21) → POST /api/upload → Go POST /v1/projects/{id}/file, and it returns exactly the fileUrl / serverPath a FloorConfig needs (src/app/api/upload/route.ts:43-74).
  • Delete: deleteFileAction(name, projectId) (src/actions/projects.ts:285-305) → Go DELETE /v1/projects/{id}/file?name=.
  • Commit: onFloorChange is already typed (floorId, patch: Partial<FloorConfig>) (EditFloorModal.tsx:33) and both hosts forward it to updateFloorConfig, which already accepts those fields (floorsSlice.ts:15).
  • Persistence: PersistedFloorConfig (wizardState.ts:20-28) already carries all three.

No Go contract change, no new API route, no new server action, no store action.

Scope

Preview — nearly free. Pass onPreview + label to the FloorThumbnail already at EditFloorModal.tsx:210-214, exactly as FloorRow.tsx:91-97 does, and mount the existing FloorPreviewModal (src/components/setup/shared/FloorPreviewModal.tsx). The wizard already builds previewItems at StepListFloor.tsx:124-134 — either lift that list into the modal or take it as a prop. Only floors that have an image should be previewable, so prev/next walks real images.

Add / change / remove. A hidden file input plus thumbnail hover actions per row, delegating upload and delete through a new prop pair so the wizard and editor hosts can differ. Put the shared handler next to uploadImage.ts in src/lib/editor/, not duplicated in both hosts.

Files touched: EditFloorModal.tsx, StepListFloor.tsx, EditLevelModal.tsx, plus one shared handler.

Hazards — read before writing code

  • Do not call addUploadedFile from the modal. StepListFloor.tsx:76-89 appends a new floorConfig for any uploadedFile whose serverPath is not yet tracked. Calling addUploadedFile (the way useAddLevel.ts:98 does) spawns a phantom floor row in the wizard. Patch the floorConfig only; do not touch uploadedFiles.
  • Change and remove must delete the old object. Follow EditLevelModal.tsx:106-113 — recover the stored name via fileNameOf, then fire-and-forget deleteFileAction. Skipping it leaks a MinIO object per swap.
  • FloorConfig.opacity is a dead field. It is persisted end to end (wizardState.ts:75,100,200) but never read — the editor backdrop uses the global floorImageOpacity (editorSlice.ts:172, default 50). Do not add a per-floor opacity slider assuming it works.
  • The editor host scopes rows to the selected building (EditLevelModal.tsx:66-71) and seeds synthetic configs for level-only floors (:82-101) whose serverPath is "". Those rows will show the add-image empty state — probably right, but look at it.
  • floorConfigs are not in the per-level collab stream (FloorplanEditor.tsx:589-600 broadcasts level snapshots only), so an image swap reaches collaborators only on save.

Needs a ruling before the remove control is built

  1. May a floor have no image at all? blockingFloors (wizardProject.ts:181-190) treats a floor with empty serverPath and no own level geometry as not ready, which disables Step 3's Continue (StepListFloor.tsx:207). Either disallow remove when it would block, or accept an image-less floor and adjust the gate.
  2. Should "change image" offer a re-scan? The traced walls live in canvasData.levels, entirely separate from fileUrl — swapping the raster leaves old geometry over a new backdrop (FloorplanEditor.tsx:602-604). The machinery exists (useAddLevel.scanAddedFloor + replaceLevelContent) but wiring it is materially bigger. Otherwise state plainly that the image is a tracing backdrop only.

Tests

New src/components/setup/step-list-floor/__tests__/EditFloorModal.image.test.tsx:

  • floor with fileUrl set → the thumbnail is a button named Preview <floor name>. Fails today: FloorThumbnail.tsx:104-109 renders a plain div, so getByRole("button", {name:/Preview/}) throws.
  • floor with fileUrl: "" → an Add image control is present and the preview button is not.
  • pick a file on a floor that already has one → onFloorChange called once with {fileUrl, serverPath, originalFileName} for that id, and deleteFileAction called with the old stored name (mock @/actions/projects the way EditLevelModal.test.ts:7 does; mock /api/upload via global.fetch).
  • remove → onFloorChange(id, {fileUrl:"", serverPath:"", originalFileName:""}) and one deleteFileAction.

Plus a readiness fence in src/lib/projects/__tests__/: a config whose serverPath is cleared but whose level has its own geometry stays out of blockingFloors; one with neither is blocking. That is the assertion that catches "remove image silently bricked Step 3's Continue".

Acceptance criteria

  • Each floor row in the Edit Floor modal can add an image when it has none, and preview / change / remove it when it has one — in both the wizard and the editor
  • Preview uses the shared FloorPreviewModal, reachable by keyboard as well as hover
  • Change and remove delete the previous file server-side
  • No phantom floor row appears in the wizard after an add or change
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Not this task

Defaulting automatic floor naming to off — checkbox 2 of #871, tracked separately.

issues.display_title: Issue #879: chore(wizard): default automatic floor naming to off (#871)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-879.mp4

Implementation task for enhancement #871, checkbox 2: "Set default automatic floor naming to 'false'".

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Why

Automatic floor naming is on by default. While it is on, useApplyFloorSettings force-rewrites every floor's name to Floor N bottom-up on every toggle, reorder, add and delete (src/hooks/useApplyFloorSettings.ts:18-28), and the modal locks the name input behind a padlock (EditFloorModal.tsx:185, :391-393). So a user opening Edit Floor for the first time cannot type a floor name until they find and flip a switch — which is what the screenshot in #871 shows.

The change

// src/lib/wizard/units.ts:14-18
export const DEFAULT_FLOOR_SETTINGS: FloorSettings = {
  autoNaming: true,   // -> false
  sameHeight: false,
  unit: "m",
};

That is the whole diff. The constant is read live as the store's initial state (floorsSlice.ts:22-25).

No migration needed. floorSettings is persisted per project (wizardState.ts:78) and hydration never consults the constant:

// src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts:217-223
const savedFloorSettings = saved.floorSettings;
const namesAreAuto = detectAutoNaming(saved.floorConfigs ?? []);
store.setFloorSettings(
  savedFloorSettings
    ? { ...savedFloorSettings, autoNaming: savedFloorSettings.autoNaming && namesAreAuto }
    : { autoNaming: namesAreAuto, sameHeight: false, unit: "m" },
);

An existing project keeps its saved value; a legacy project with no saved slice keeps its detected value.

Floors are still named. StepListFloor.tsx:62-72 and :76-89 seed autoNameFor(i) at upload regardless of the toggle. Turning the default off does not leave floors unnamed — it makes the name field typeable and stops the automatic renumbering.

Knock-ons

  • src/store/__tests__/useMapStore-importedFloorSettings.test.ts:10-13 is the one test that pins the current default. Both assertions invert to toBe(false), and its title ("auto-naming is on by default, which is what clobbered imported names") needs rewriting — it documents #626's cause, which this change removes.
  • keepImportedFloorSettings (floorsSlice.ts:62-63, from #626) now only has sameHeight left to turn off. Leaving it as-is is correct and safer than trimming it.

Needs a ruling

wizardState.ts:222 is a second, independent default — the legacy fallback literal, whose autoNaming is detected from the stored names. Flipping DEFAULT_FLOOR_SETTINGS does not touch it, so a legacy project whose floors are all named Floor N still hydrates with auto-naming on. Leave it (cheaper, and matches "existing projects keep the old value") or force it false too?

Tests

  • Invert src/store/__tests__/useMapStore-importedFloorSettings.test.ts:10-13 and its title.
  • Add to src/lib/persistence/__tests__/wizardState.test.ts (its hydrateWith helper at 140-157 is the right harness): "a project that saved autoNaming: true over auto names still hydrates true after the default flip" — hydrate [{name:"Floor 1"},{name:"Floor 2"}] with {autoNaming:true,…}, expect .autoNaming toBe(true). This fails if someone "migrates" by forcing false on load, and proves no migration is needed.

Acceptance criteria

  • A new project opens Edit Floor with Automatic floor naming off and the name field editable
  • Existing projects keep whatever they saved
  • New floors are still created named Floor N
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Not this task

Floor image add / preview / change / remove — checkbox 1 of #871, tracked separately.

issues.display_title: Issue #889: fix(map): an Area renders as building massing in Overview, and a Closed room's corners paint grey (#884)
issues.main_description_html:
Reported in #884 (video feedback), two defects:

  • Reduce the height of the area, and change the area's color to #ececec
  • Glitching corner closed room

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause 1 — an Area is drawn as building massing

outdoorGeoJson (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:1385) turns every ring of the shell floor's layout.areas into an outdoor-shell feature extruded to the building's whole stacked height:

const rings: LngLatTuple[][] =
  ground.layout.areas.length > 0
    ? ground.layout.areas.map((a) => { /* … */ })   // ← no filter of any kind
    : [[ /* bbox corners */ ]];

Since #839 a standalone Area the user drew lives in that same array, told apart only by AreaLayer.manual. Nothing on the render path has ever read that flag — a repo-wide grep finds readers only in the 2D editor engine and the object panel. So a car park drawn beside a mall is extruded to the mall's own height and painted the same slate #8e97ab (layer-definitions.ts:327), which is exactly the issue title.

In Overview this is the only geometry on screen: viewerBuildingSplit returns { indoor: [], outer: all } (viewerBuildings.ts:64), and PreviewOverlay passes visible: !outdoor to the indoor layers.

Root cause 2 — a Closed room's corners paint themselves grey

Each wall vertex gets a disc (an extruded cylinder sized to the wall's half-thickness) that fills the notch where two segments meet. The wall strips carry the closed-room treatment:

const wallProps = wallColor
  ? { areaColor: wallColor, areaColorDark: outlineFor(wallColor, 0.35), closedAreaId: levelAreaIds[ownerIdx!] }
  : {};

The discs did not:

properties: { id: `${level.level_id}_wj${ji++}`, type: "wall", height: topH, base_height: baseH, isActive }

A disc is type: "wall", so it renders through fp-wall-extrusion-active, fp-wall-cap-active and fp-wall-base-active — whose closedColor() coalesce falls through to WALL_COLOR #ebeae7 and WALL_TOP_COLOR #9b9994 when those keys are absent. Result: a grey half-moon poking out of every corner of a tinted room, and the hatching beside it, which is the same two colours z-fighting over the footprint the disc and the strip share by construction.

Fix

  1. Area pad. A manual area keeps its footprint and loses the storeys: OUTDOOR_AREA_HEIGHT = 0.5 m (a kerb, not a storey — the shortest possible building shell is one 3 m floor), painted #ececec through a new shellColor the shell layer coalesces on.

    It stays type: "outdoor-shell" deliberately. That layer's id is what SHELL_GUARD_LAYERS (the editor's building-drag guard) and useOutdoorMode's click-to-enter handler are both bound to, so a tidier new type would silently take a press over an Area out of both. A click on the car park still walks into the building it serves, exactly as today.

    coalesce, not case: a bare ["get", …] as a case condition throws on the buildings that carry no such property and MapLibre falls back to the paint default — evaluated against the repo's own style-spec, that renders every shell black.

  2. Corner discs. The disc now carries the same { areaColor, areaColorDark, closedAreaId } the strips do. A corner shared with a plain wall goes to the room, not to whichever wall happens to be thicker — matching the "first closed room wins" tie-break closedWallOwners already makes. No wallId on the disc: it belongs to every wall meeting there, and naming one would count it among that wall's strips.

Heights are untouched. The hatching was never a geometry bug — it is the colour mismatch made visible, and it goes with the colour.

Verification

Gate Result
new tests 4, all 4 red on development
pnpm test 215 files, 2016 passed
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean
pnpm lint clean
paint expression evaluated against @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec

Filmed before/after on one project across two dev servers (development vs this branch). Every fill-extrusion pixel carries a uniform +7 lighting offset, so the sampled colours land on the constants exactly:

Sample Measured −7 Constant
car park, before #959eb2 #8e97ab OUTDOOR_SHELL_COLOR
car park, after #f3f3f3 #ececec OUTDOOR_AREA_COLOR
room corner, before #a2a09b #9b9994 WALL_TOP_COLOR — the grey nub
room corner, after #525f79 — the room's own blue, under the slab gradient

Known gap

manual is stamped only by the 2D editor's modelToLevel. A Mappedin/AI-imported parking polygon carries no manual flag (mappedin/convert.ts:466), so it keeps massing until that level is round-tripped through the Floorplan tab. If the project in the report came from an import and was never re-saved, opening and saving the floor is what applies the fix to it.

Out of scope, found while tracing

  • Routing still detours around Areas — buildingSolidsPx shares the same rings and feeds the outdoor grid as obstacles. Deliberately untouched.
  • buildingIdAtLngLat and the camera fit both read levelBBox, which a large Area inflates, so Overview zoom-in can enter a building from over its car park and the fit frames wider than the building.

Demo

.playwright-mcp/demo/884/video-884-area-and-corners.mp4 — 1920×1080, 60 fps, 106 s, NVENC on the Tesla P4.

One project, two dev servers: development unfixed vs this branch. Each build gets one page load and one camera move — in close on a Closed room's corner, then out to Overview. Stills beside it: final-corner.png, final-overview.png.

Rebuild the subject with 884/setup.mjs (creates a scratch project: a Closed room with 400 mm walls beside an Area the size of a car park), then:

DEMO_BASE_URL=http://localhost:6084 DEMO_BEFORE_URL=http://localhost:6060 \
DEMO_PROJECT_ID=<id> ./record.sh 884 area-and-corners

The scenario asserts rather than trusting the camera — it throws if Overview never engages, or if zooming back in drops out of it.

In main via #891 (96ad773) — merged through #890 (3eae2ce) on development. Commit 6e0cd95.

issues.display_title: Issue #880: fix(editor): drawing a wall along an existing one appends a second wall instead of reusing it (#872)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-880.mp4

Implementation task for bug #872. The report is a screen recording with no text; the repro below is read frame by frame off that video, and the mechanism is traced in code.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Repro

Project Kuwait (Sample), floor Main 2, /editor/ea57d61d-2e19-48d4-bb9a-000f71f16cd4, object count All 45. The plan is rotated, so every wall runs at a slight angle.

  1. Draw a new room in the open ground to the left of the existing lower-right room, closing a four-corner ring. Count goes 45 → 50 — four walls plus one detected room, listed as Room 5.
  2. Drag the new room's right-hand wall up against the existing room's left wall until they are flush.
  3. Zoom in. There are two walls with a white gap between them, and two separate nodes at each end. They never become one wall.

The 32 px / 33 px badge visible in the recording is just the hovered wall's length (draw.ts:199 → fmtLen, which falls back to ${Math.round(u)} px on an uncalibrated project). Not a distance, not a thickness.

What actually happens

Nothing in the engine ever asks "is there already a wall here?" before pushing one. There are exactly two places that push:

// src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/interaction-tools.ts:118-123  (finishWall — the draw path, this report)
for (const v of pts) splitWallAt(ctx, v);            // W-2: split where new vertices land on walls
for (let i = 0; i < pts.length - 1; i++) {
  const a = pts[i], b = pts[i + 1];
  if (Math.abs(a[0] - b[0]) < 0.5 && Math.abs(a[1] - b[1]) < 0.5) continue;
  model.walls.push({ x1: a[0], y1: a[1], x2: b[0], y2: b[1], l: "0", r: "0" });
}
// src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/commands.ts:263-265  (convertAreaToRoom — #865)
pushUndo(ctx);
// Appended, never spliced in: store wall ids are positional.
model.walls.push(...edges);

The two existing "attach" behaviours do not cover this:

  • wallPoint (interaction-tools.ts:64-69) projects each click onto an existing node (HANDLE_R = 9) or wall centreline (WALL_SNAP_RADIUS_PX = 8) — both screen px, so the pull shrinks in world units as you zoom in, and past the radius nothing happens at all.
  • splitWallAt (interaction-tools.ts:97) cuts an existing wall where a new vertex lands in its interior, within 0.5 world units. It handles vertices, never whole edges, and it never removes or reuses a wall. In this recording it fired zero times — that is what 45 → 50 exactly means.

So two walls end up describing one physical wall. Cost, measured:

  • one redundant row per duplicated wall in the object list (objectRows.ts:181 emits one row per layout.walls entry) and one redundant extrusion on the map
  • the two rooms are not neighbours in the model, because the two edges never fuse
  • the visible hairline gap the reporter zoomed in on

What does not happen, and should not be written into the fix: an exactly-duplicated wall does not split a face. detectRooms keys edges by fused node pair and collapses coincident chords (rooms.ts:217-234, under the comment "a ring converted on top of walls that already exist … must not double the edge and split the face in two"). Probed: a 4-wall room plus an exact duplicate of its bottom wall plus a ring below on that same line gives 8 walls and 2 correct rooms, no sliver. A phantom face needs a near-miss divergence that is enclosed at both ends and wider than TOL = 1 mean width (rooms.ts:338) — measured: a 2.5-unit detour over a 20-unit stretch yields a 25 unit² phantom; a 1.5-unit detour yields none.

Scope

One shared helper, both call sites. Put "is there already a straight wall along a..b?" in src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts next to doorSpanOnWall (geometry.ts:264), which is already the collinear-and-overlapping primitive — normalised-cross parallelism plus per-endpoint perpendicular distance. It clips its span to [0,1], so a reuse check that must also extend a wall should call the primitive underneath it, projectOnWall (geometry.ts:253). Export through floorplan/index.ts.

Then:

  1. finishWall — run it after the existing splitWallAt pass, so a partially covered edge is already cut into pieces that either match or do not. Skip the push for a matched segment; extend the matched wall where the new edge runs past its end.
  2. convertAreaToRoom — the same filter over edges, which is #865. Its dry run (commands.ts:253) must filter identically or it validates a ring the commit no longer builds.

finishCurveWall (interaction-tools.ts:128) is the third walls.push and is deliberately out of scope — a curve has no straight span to reuse, and splitWallAt:101 already skips h1x !== undefined for the same reason.

Extending in place is safe: wall ids are positional (bridge.ts:368 maps model.walls 1:1 by index), so mutating a wall preserves its id, and skipping a push only appends fewer walls — no splice, no reindex. wallForOpening / doorSpanOnWall clip to [0,1], so a door on the original span still resolves after the wall is lengthened. Undo is a whole-model JSON snapshot (history.ts:12, :120) under the single existing pushUndo, so an extension reverses as cleanly as an append.

Needs a ruling

  1. The tolerance, and its space. It cannot be TOL = 1 — at 1 unit the endpoints already fuse and edgeAt already collapses the edge, so a 1-unit tolerance changes nothing visible. It has to be ~2–3 units to catch what this report shows. Above 1 unit it welds geometry the user can see as two separate walls. Screen px means the same gesture merges or does not depending on zoom; world units is stable but arbitrary across plan scales. Pick one, write it down next to TOL, and say what it costs.
  2. Silent or announced. A wall the user just drew not appearing in the object list is surprising unless the status line says why ("reused Wall 12").
  3. Shared walls mean shared deletes. Two rooms that share a boundary end up sharing one wall record — correct digital-twin semantics, and what makes them neighbours — but deleting that wall then opens both rooms.

Tests

New src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/finish-wall-reuse.test.ts, modelled on wall-point-priority.test.ts (identity view, devicePixelRatio = 1). All "today" numbers below are measured against current development:

  1. No duplicate wall. Existing square of 4 walls; draw [[0,0],[0,-100],[200,-100],[200,0],[0,0]] sharing the top edge. Today 8 walls; assert 7.
  2. Reversed direction is the same wall. The same edge traced the other way must still be reused, not duplicated.
  3. Extend, do not truncate. Existing wall (0,0)-(100,0); draw a ring whose bottom edge runs (0,0)-(200,0). Assert wall 0 still starts at (0,0) and now ends at x2: 200, and the wall count is 4, not 5.
  4. Near-miss stays two walls. A room drawn 2 units inside another — today 8 walls and a 400 unit² phantom room. Assert the chosen tolerance's outcome; this is the case that pins ruling 1.
  5. Regression fence. A room drawn in open ground far from any wall still yields exactly 4 walls and 1 detected room.

Add the convertAreaToRoom half to src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/convert-area-to-room.test.ts — see #865.

Acceptance criteria

  • Drawing a wall along an existing wall reuses it instead of appending a second one, and extends it where the new edge overruns
  • Two rooms drawn flush against each other are neighbours in the model, with one wall between them and no hairline gap
  • A conversion or a drawing that touches nothing existing behaves exactly as before
  • Undo reverses the whole gesture in one step, including any extension
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Related

Same root cause as #865, different entry point. commands.ts:265 and interaction-tools.ts:122 are the only two walls.push sites and both are missing the same lookup. Whichever lands first should write the shared helper; the other becomes call-site wiring plus tests. They should ship together.

Found while tracing, not this task — worth their own reports:

  • JOIN_EPS = 3 (constants.ts:5) is in world units while every sibling tolerance is screen px (hittest.ts:11, editing.ts:28). selectTarget arms every wall drag through joinGroup (interactions.ts:381), so zooming in never separates two corners 3 units apart — dragging one always drags the neighbour's.
  • The nearestWallPoint pull is invisible and unrefusable: addSnap, the only snap cue drawn (draw.ts:210-211), comes from hitHandle only, and both snaps return before the Shift/Alt branches in wallPoint, so no modifier bypasses them.

Verification

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

RESCOPED — the report is a drag, not a drawing

The task as written scoped the fix to finishWall, on the draw path. That was built, measured against unmodified development on the real editor, and found completely inert — identical object counts at every offset (see the comment above). wallPoint already snaps every click to an existing handle (HANDLE_R = 9) or wall centreline (WALL_SNAP_RADIUS_PX = 8), unrefusably, and node fusion (TOL = 1) already collapses the edge. Drawing a room exactly flush against another already adds three walls, not four, on development today.

Re-reading #872: step 1 draws a room in open ground (45 → 50, correct). The duplicate appears at step 2, dragging the new room's wall onto the existing one. That path — endPointer — is what this now fixes.

Reproduced at unit level on development first:

before      walls=8 rooms=2   B's right wall (250,50)-(250,250)
after-exact walls=8 rooms=2   now (300,50)-(300,250) — exactly on top of A's left wall
after-2short walls=8          298 — two separate nodes at each end, past TOL = 1

RESULT

Branch feature/880-wall-drag-merge, three commits off development (3eae2ce).

weldMovedWalls (src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/editing.ts), called from weldDraggedWalls in endPointer — before recomputeRooms, so detection sees the merged geometry, and after the drag's own pushUndo, so move and weld reverse in one step. Two steps, only the second removes anything:

  1. Straighten. Every endpoint of the dragged wall moves to its foot on the found wall's line, and to that wall's own corner when one is within tolerance, carrying the endpoints that sit on it. This is what closes the gap under the one unit detectRooms fuses on — and that, measured, is what makes the two rooms neighbours. Removing the duplicate record does not buy the neighbour relation; closing the gap does.
  2. Fold. If the dragged wall now describes the same span, the duplicate record goes. The wall kept is the one that was already there, since modelToLevel mints wall ids positionally.

A partial overlap keeps both records on purpose: two walls of different lengths sharing part of their run are two walls, and the face walk already gives the shared stretch one edge. The found wall is never extended — an extended endpoint leaves its JOIN_EPS weld group at a shared corner, which is what #722 exists to prevent, and where two collinear walls tie it would stretch one over its own sibling and manufacture a fresh duplicate.

Ruling 1 — the tolerance, and its space

Screen px, not world units: px(WALL_SNAP_RADIUS_PX) / ctx.sc — the same eight pixels wallPoint snaps a click within, so the two gestures obey one rule.

An absolute three units was tried first and is wrong here: it is three screen pixels at 1:1 but a quarter of one with a whole floor on screen, where nobody can land a drag that precisely — the fix would have gone quietly inert at exactly the zoom people lay a floor out at. That is the same shape of mistake that made the first attempt inert.

The cost, plainly: zoomed far out, eight pixels is a lot of plan, and a wall dragged until it visibly overlaps another becomes that wall. Zoomed in it is very little, and a wall parked a hand's width away stays put. The tolerance tracks what the user can see, because seeing is what they aim with. Ctrl+Z is the way back.

Ruling 2 — announced, but the editor has nowhere to say it

The engine emits merged into the wall already there on the status line. It is not visible. FloorplanEditor.tsx:817 renders status only when statusErr is true — every non-error status(...) in the engine goes nowhere in this UI, this one included. Raising it as an error would be wrong (red, and it fires reportEditBlocked telemetry), and adding a neutral toast would surface every informational status the engine already emits. Left as a separate UI gap, not built here. In practice the drag case is more self-evident than the draw case the ruling was written for: the user is actively pushing one wall onto another, and the wall count in the object list moves.

Ruling 3 — shared walls mean shared deletes

Live and unflagged: after the weld the two rooms share one wall record, so Del on it opens both. That is correct digital-twin semantics and is the point of the change, but nothing distinguishes the merged wall from any other in the selection line.

What an adversarial pass caught before this shipped

Three ways the first cut destroyed work. All three reproduced; each guard is load-bearing for exactly one, verified by disabling it and watching that case come back.

  • A room narrowed to within the tolerance was annihilated. One room, drag its left wall right until eight units of daylight remain — the commonest edit there is. The room's own right wall answered as the wall to fold into and the two walls between them were carried down to nothing: 4 walls → 3, two of them zero length, 0 rooms. The weld now works out where every endpoint would land before writing any of it and refuses the whole fold if it would leave another wall shorter than a point.
  • The weld fired on where a wall ended up, not on what the drag did. Two parallel walls 28 units apart at quarter zoom — seven screen pixels, two visibly separate lines, geometry nobody had just made. Nudge one along its own length, so the perpendicular gap never changes, and it was folded into a neighbour it never approached. The drag now records where each wall stood at commit; a wall already lying along its candidate is left alone.
  • The weld gathered a corner on a tighter epsilon than the drag did. The drag groups on JOIN_EPS = 3 and detectRooms closes a ring within 1, so a corner 0.7 out of true is one corner to both — but the weld's 0.5 sweep moved half of it and tore the room open. The caller now hands its own grouping rule in.

Known and left standing

  • Dragging a wall with a door onto another wall with a door at the same place leaves both doors, stacked on the merged wall — the state dragBrokeOpenings refuses mid-drag. Refusing the fold does not help (two coincident doors on two coincident walls); the alternative is deleting one of the user's doors.
  • Where the target wall was cut in two by a T-junction, reusableWall matches one half and the fold does not fire — the gap still closes, the duplicate record survives.
  • Acceptance criterion 1 (the draw path) is deliberately not met. It is already satisfied by the click-time snapping, measured. finishWall still pushes unconditionally and should stay that way; #865 covers the conversion half.
